s: Under which Article is the National Commission for Backward Classes provided for?
x: The NCSC, NCST and NCBC fall under Articles 338, 338A and 338B respectively.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment created the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
x: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990 created the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 338.

s: The combined commission created by the 65th Amendment replaced the Special Officer and the commission set up by the Resolution of which year?
x: The 65th Amendment (1990) commission replaced the original Special Officer for SCs and STs and the commission set up by the 1987 Resolution.

s: Which one of the following was a consequence of the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018?
o: Bifurcation of the NCSC and NCST
Insertion of Article 338B and constitutional status for the NCBC
Insertion of Article 350B and creation of the Linguistic Minorities Officer
Creation of the first statutory NCBC
x: The 102nd Amendment inserted Article 338B and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The other developments belong to different constitutional provisions or earlier enactments.

s: For which separate body did the creation of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in 1999 pave the way?
x: The separate Ministry of Tribal Affairs set up in 1999 paved the way for a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

s: Which of the following was another effect of the 102nd Constitutional Amendment?
o: Transferring all SEBC-list powers to State Governors
Removing Scheduled Tribes from the purview of the NCST
Removing backward classes from the purview of the NCSC
x: The 102nd Amendment removed backward classes from the purview of the NCSC while constitutionalising the NCBC under Article 338B.

s: When was the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes set up?
x: The NCST under Article 338A was set up on 19 February 2004 after the 89th Amendment.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment restored the States' power to prepare their own lists of SEBCs?
x: The 105th Amendment, 2021 restored the States' power; the 102nd Amendment had let the President notify SEBCs.

s: Under the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018, who notifies the socially and educationally backward classes (SEBCs)?
x: The 102nd Amendment gave the NCBC constitutional status and made the President notify SEBCs; the 105th Amendment later restored States' own lists.

s: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
x: The NCW is statutory (NCW Act, 1990); the NCST (338A), NCBC (338B) and Finance Commission (280) are constitutional.

s: Who appoints the members of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?
o: President by warrant under his hand and seal
x: The President appoints the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members by warrant under his hand and seal.

s: Besides the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson, the constitutional NCBC has how many members?
x: The constitutional NCBC has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members; the earlier statutory NCBC had five members.

s: What is the term of the members of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes under the rules?
x: Members serve a term of 3 years under the rules; tenure and service conditions are fixed by the President.

s: Who was to head the statutory National Commission for Backward Classes set up under the 1993 Act?
o: A retired judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court
x: The statutory NCBC of 1993 had five members headed by a retired Supreme Court or High Court judge.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the National Commissions for the protected communities?
o: Inquiring into specific complaints of deprivation of rights
Investigating and monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards
Adjudicating criminal cases and awarding punishment to offenders
Advising on socio-economic planning and evaluating progress
x: The Commissions investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on development; they do not function as criminal courts or award criminal punishment.

s: To whom are the annual and special reports of the National Commissions for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes submitted?
x: The annual and special reports of these constitutional commissions are submitted to the President. The President lays them before Parliament along with an action-taken memorandum.

s: Under Article 338(9), which one of the following is required of the Union and every State Government?
o: They must transfer their powers over Scheduled Caste lists to the Commission.
They must consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on major policy matters affecting Scheduled Castes.
They must obtain the Commission's prior approval for every welfare expenditure.
They must consult the Commission only on matters concerning Union Territories.
x: Article 338(9) requires the Union and every State Government to consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on all major policy matters affecting Scheduled Castes. It does not confer prior approval or list-alteration powers on the Commission.

s: Before a proposal for de-reservation of posts is implemented, which body must first examine it?
o: NCSC, NCST or NCBC, as applicable
x: Proposals for de-reservation of posts must first be examined by the relevant NCSC, NCST or NCBC, depending on the category concerned.

s: Which one of the following is specifically associated with the functions of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Appointment of State Human Rights Commissioners
Protection of minor forest produce ownership and tribal mineral and water rights
x: The NCST deals, among other matters, with ownership of minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribal communities.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Commissions for SCs and STs?
o: They can punish those who violate safeguards
State-related reports go to the Governor
Governments must consult them on major policy matters
x: The Commissions are not criminal courts and have no power to punish; their recommendations are advisory.

s: While investigating a matter, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes has the powers of which court?
x: It has civil-court powers: summoning persons, requiring documents, receiving affidavits, requisitioning records and issuing commissions for witnesses.

s: Where are the civil-court powers of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes provided?
x: Article 338(8) gives the NCSC civil-court powers; Article 338(9) is about mandatory consultation.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional NCBC?
o: It is appointed by State Governors and exercises the powers of a tribunal.
It is appointed by the President and possesses powers of a civil court.
It is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and possesses criminal-court powers.
It is appointed by the Prime Minister and functions only as an advisory body without legal powers.
x: The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members of the constitutional NCBC are appointed by the President, and the Commission has civil-court powers.

s: In 2026, which commission began a full review of proposals relating to de-reservation of posts?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
x: In August 2026, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes began a full review of proposals relating to de-reservation of posts.

s: Who was the first chairperson of the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes constituted in 2004?
x: Kunwar Singh was the first NCST chairperson (2004); Suraj Bhan headed the first separate NCSC and S.H. Ramdhan the combined commission (1992).

s: As of 2026, who heads the National Commission for Backward Classes?
x: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed Chairperson of the NCBC in 2026. Harjit Singh Grewal heads the National Commission for Minorities. Kunwar Singh and Suraj Bhan were the first chairpersons of the NCST and NCSC respectively.

s: Who is the present Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?
x: Kishor Makwana heads the NCSC (from March 2024); Suraj Bhan was its first chairperson.

s: Who was the first Chairperson of the combined National Commission for SCs and STs (1992)?
x: S.H. Ramdhan was the first chair of the combined commission; Suraj Bhan and Kunwar Singh were the first chairs of the separate NCSC and NCST.

s: Who is the present Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
x: Antar Singh Arya heads the NCST; Kishor Makwana heads the NCSC and Niranjan Jyoti the NCBC.

s: Who became the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026?
x: Harjit Singh Grewal became NCM Chairperson on 21 July 2026.

s: Which of the following pairs (Commission – Present Chairperson) is wrongly matched?
o: National Commission for Women – Vijaya Rahatkar
National Human Rights Commission – Justice V. Ramasubramanian
National Commission for Scheduled Castes – Antar Singh Arya
National Commission for Scheduled Tribes – Antar Singh Arya
x: Kishor Makwana chairs the NCSC; Antar Singh Arya chairs the NCST.

s: Which of the following pairs (Commission – first Chairperson) is correctly matched?
x: Justice R.N. Prasad (1993) was the first chairperson of the statutory NCBC (Bhagwan Lal Sahni was first of the constitutional NCBC, 2019); the first chairs of NCW, NHRC and NCM were Jayanti Patnaik, Ranganath Misra and Mohd. Sardar Ali Khan.

s: Who was the first Chairperson of the constitutional National Commission for Backward Classes (2019)?
x: Bhagwan Lal Sahni was the first Chairperson of the constitutional NCBC; Justice R.N. Prasad headed the statutory NCBC of 1993.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Article 350B is correct?
o: It creates the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
It enables the President to recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of a State.
It permits grievances to be submitted only in the official language of the Union.
It guarantees mother-tongue instruction in all stages of education.
x: Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, also known as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.

s: Which Article provides for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for linguistic minority children?
x: Article 350A directs States to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage; Article 350B is the Special Officer.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?
x: Its headquarters is New Delhi; it moved there from Allahabad in 2015.

s: To whom does the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities submit reports?
x: The Special Officer reports to the President, who lays the reports before Parliament and sends them to the States.

s: Which Amendment inserted Article 350B on the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?
x: Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956.

s: Under which Ministry does the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities work?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities works under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, with headquarters in New Delhi.

s: What did the Supreme Court uphold, among other things, in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, decided on 16 November 1992?
o: 27 per cent reservation for OBCs and the concept of the creamy layer
50 per cent reservation exclusively for economically weaker sections
The abolition of all reservation in public employment
The exclusive power of States to notify all SEBCs without constitutional limitation
x: The judgment upheld 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, introduced the creamy-layer principle and directed the creation of a permanent body concerning inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.

s: The direction in Indra Sawhney concerning a permanent body for inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list led to the establishment of which body?
o: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under the 89th Amendment
National Commission for Women under the 1990 Act
Statutory National Commission for Backward Classes under the 1993 Act
National Commission for Minorities under the 1992 Act
x: The direction in Indra Sawhney led to the NCBC Act, 1993 and the establishment of the statutory NCBC. It was intended to advise on inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.

s: Who headed the first Backward Classes Commission, set up in 1953?
x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the first Backward Classes Commission (1953); B.P. Mandal chaired the second.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First National Commission for Backward Classes – 1951
First constitutional recognition of OBC reservation – 1993
First State to introduce reservation – Kolhapur
First constitutional recognition of OBC reservation – 102nd Amendment
x: Kolhapur was the first State to introduce reservation; the 1st Amendment (1951) first recognised OBC reservation and the first NCBC came in 1993.

s: Which government appointed the Second Backward Classes Commission headed by B.P. Mandal?
x: The Mandal Commission was appointed on 1 January 1979 by the Janata government of Morarji Desai.

s: Which Backward Classes Commission was the first to recommend 27% reservation for OBCs?
x: The Mandal Commission (1979) was the first to recommend 27% OBC reservation.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment added Article 15(4), the first amendment on reservations?
x: Article 15(4) was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951, the first amendment on reservations.

s: In which year was the Second Backward Classes Commission under B.P. Mandal appointed?
x: The Mandal Commission was appointed on 1 January 1979 by the Janata government.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution were the Kaka Kalelkar and B.P. Mandal Backward Classes Commissions appointed?
x: Both Backward Classes Commissions (1953 and 1979) were appointed by the President under Art. 340.

s: How was NITI Aayog set up?
x: NITI Aayog is an executive body set up by a Cabinet resolution of 1 January 2015.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis:
1. It was originally a statutory body under a 1993 Act.
2. Its Act lapsed on 29 February 2004.
3. It is now a constitutional body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The NCSK Act of 1993 lapsed on 29 February 2004; since then the NCSK has been extended as a non-statutory body.

s: What is the legal status of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Statutory body under the NCM Act
Executive body set up by a Cabinet resolution
x: The NCM is a statutory body under the NCM Act; it has no Article of the Constitution behind it.

s: In which year was the separate Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Tribes Act passed?
x: The AP State Commission for Scheduled Tribes Act is of 2020; the Assembly passed separate SC and ST Bills in December 2019.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for SCs and STs created by a State Act?
x: The AP State Commission for SCs and STs was created by a 2003 State Act; it was later split into separate SC and ST commissions.

s: Under which of the following is the National Commission for Women a statutory body?
x: The NCW is statutory under the NCW Act, 1990; there is no Article 338C. Article 338B is the NCBC.

s: When was the National Commission for Women constituted?
x: The NCW was constituted in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.

s: Which of the following powers does the National Commission for Women NOT have?
x: The NCW can appoint committees, co-opt outsiders and regulate its own procedure, but cannot impose criminal sentences.

s: Who nominates the Chairperson, Members and Member-Secretary of the National Commission for Women?
x: All of them are nominated by the Central Government, not appointed by the President.

s: In the context of women's rights, what does 'Jan Sunwai' refer to?
o: An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
A public hearing of women’s grievances
A legislative session on gender budgeting
x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings held to hear and address women’s grievances.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Women?
o: Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
x: The NCW reviews laws, suggests amendments, takes suo motu notice and commissions special studies; it does not enforce criminal sentences imposed by courts.

s: What does Section 10 of the National Commission for Women Act, 1990 deal with?
x: Section 10 of the NCW Act lists the functions of the Commission, such as reviewing laws and looking into complaints.

s: Besides the Chairperson and the Member-Secretary, how many members does the National Commission for Women have?
x: The NCW has a Chairperson, five members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Women:
1. Besides the Chairperson, it has five members, of whom at least one must be from the SCs and one from the STs.
2. Its Chairperson and members are appointed by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NCW has a Chairperson, five members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary, all nominated by the Central Government, not the President.

s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?
x: Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW Chairperson; Vijaya Rahatkar is the present one.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The NCBC acquired constitutional status under the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018, and Article 338B. The 89th Amendment Act, 2003, relates to the separation of the NCSC and NCST.

s: Which statement regarding the National Human Rights Commission is correct?
o: It is a Statutory Body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
It is a Constitutional Body governed by Article 263.
It is a Constitutional Body governed by Article 338.
It is an Extra-Constitutional Body established by a Cabinet Resolution.
x: The NHRC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It has no Article of the Constitution behind it.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Human Rights Commission — Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Central Information Commission — Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
x: The NHRC and SHRCs come from the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Lokpal comes from the 2013 Act, the NGT from the 2010 Act and the CIC from the RTI Act, 2005.

s: When was the National Human Rights Commission set up?
x: The NHRC was set up on 12 October 1993 under the PHRA, 1993, following an ordinance of 28 September 1993.

s: After the 2019 amendment, what is the term of office of the NHRC Chairperson and members?
o: Five years or until the age of 70
Three years or until the age of 70
Three years or until the age of 65
Five years or until the age of 65
x: Since 2019 the term is three years or until 70, whichever is earlier; earlier it was five years.

s: The Chairperson of which body was added as a deemed member of the NHRC by the 2019 amendment?
x: The 2019 amendment added the NCBC and NCPCR chairpersons and the Chief Commissioner for PwD; the NCW, NCM and NCSC chairs were already deemed members.

s: Who chairs the selection committee for appointing the NHRC Chairperson and members?
x: The Prime Minister chairs the six-member committee, which includes the Union Home Minister and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the removal of the Chairperson or a member of the NHRC on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity?
o: Removal by the Prime Minister on the advice of the selection committee
Removal by the President after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
Removal by Parliament through a special-majority resolution only
Removal by the Central Government by a simple order
x: For misbehaviour or incapacity, the President removes an NHRC member after the Supreme Court inquires into the charge. A is wrong because the PM chairs the selection committee but does not remove anyone. C is wrong because no parliamentary resolution is needed. D describes the NCW, whose members the Centre can remove.

s: After the 2019 amendment, who can be appointed Chairperson of the NHRC?
o: Only a former Chief Justice of India
A former CJI or a former Judge of the Supreme Court
A former Chief Justice of a High Court
Any former Judge of a High Court
x: Since 2019 the NHRC chair can be a former CJI or a Supreme Court Judge; earlier only a former CJI.

s: After the 2019 amendment, the NHRC has how many human-rights members (at least one a woman)?
x: The 2019 amendment raised human-rights members from 2 to 3, at least one a woman.

s: The NHRC conforms to which international principles?
x: The NHRC conforms to the Paris Principles (Paris, Oct 1991; UNGA 20 Dec 1993).

s: After the 2019 amendment, human-rights work of which Union Territory stays with the NHRC?
x: The Centre may give UT human-rights work to SHRCs, but Delhi stays with the NHRC.

s: Who is the common Chairman of the Zonal Councils?
x: The Union Home Minister chairs all the Zonal Councils.

s: Where is the headquarters of the National Human Rights Commission?
x: The NHRC, set up on 12 October 1993, has its headquarters in Delhi.

s: What is the nature of the recommendations of the National Human Rights Commission?
o: Not binding, though the government must respond
x: NHRC recommendations are not binding; the government must respond but the Commission cannot compel implementation.

s: The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after what period from the date of the alleged violation?
x: The NHRC cannot inquire into a complaint after one year from the date of the alleged violation.

s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission?
x: Justice Ranganath Misra was the first NHRC chair; Mohd. Sardar Ali Khan was the first NCM chair.

s: Which body was set up in 2007 under a law enacted in 2005?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.

s: Under which Act is the NCPCR established as a statutory body?
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
x: The NCPCR was established under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, although it monitors the implementation of several other child-related laws.

s: The NCPCR monitors the implementation of which of the following Acts?
o: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
x: The NCPCR monitors the POCSO Act, 2012, along with the RTE Act, 2009 and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.

s: In which year was CEDAW adopted?
x: CEDAW was adopted in 1979; the Convention against Torture followed in 1984.

s: The NCPCR's mandate includes examining whether laws and policies conform to which of the following?
o: Paris Agreement and the Constitution alone
Convention against Torture and the Geneva Conventions
Constitution of India and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights alone
x: The NCPCR keeps laws and policies in line with the Constitution and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. India acceded to the UNCRC in 1992.

s: In which year did India accede to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child?
x: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in 1989, and India acceded to it in 1992.

s: In which year was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted?
x: The UDHR was adopted on 10 December 1948; CEDAW is 1979, the Convention against Torture 1984 and the UNCRC 1989.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Document)
A. CEDAW
B. Convention against Torture
C. UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
List-II (Year)
1. 1979
2. 1984
3. 1989
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: CEDAW was adopted in 1979, the Convention against Torture in 1984 and the UNCRC in 1989.

s: Which section of the RTE Act, 2009 provides for 25% free seats for children of weaker sections in private schools?
x: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act reserves 25% seats; the NCPCR monitors the RTE Act.

s: Which of the following pairs regarding the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis is correctly matched?
o: Governing Act now in force — NCSK Act, 1993
x: The NCSK Act, 1993 lapsed in 2004, after which the NCSK continued as a non-statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: Which of the following functions is associated with the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis?
o: Monitoring the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013
Conducting the census of urban households
Appointing municipal commissioners in every State
x: The NCSK monitors implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reports to the Government.

s: Under which Ministry does the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis function?
x: The NCSK is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, not the MWCD.

s: In which year was a Minorities Commission first set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs?
x: A Minorities Commission was set up by an MHA resolution in 1978; it became statutory under the NCM Act, 1992.

s: In which year was the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis first constituted?
x: The NCSK Act was passed in 1993 and the Commission was constituted in 1994; the Act lapsed in 2004.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NCM members – appointed by the President
NCM members – appointed by the Central Government
NCW members – appointed by the President
NCM members from minority communities – three
x: NCM members are appointed by the Central Government; five of its seven members, including the Chairperson, are from minority communities.

s: In which year were Jains notified as a minority community at the national level?
x: Jains were the latest community to be notified as a national minority, in 2014.

s: How many communities have been notified as minorities by the Government of India?
x: Six communities are notified as minorities: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis, with Jains added on 27 January 2014 as the latest notified minority.

s: What is the total strength of the National Commission for Minorities, including the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson?
x: The NCM has a Chair, a Vice-Chair and 5 members, making 7.

s: In which year was the post of Vice-Chairperson added to the National Commission for Minorities?
x: The Vice-Chairperson post was added in 1995.

s: How many States have State Minorities Commissions?
x: There are 15 State Minorities Commissions, including Andhra Pradesh.

s: In which year was the NCM Act, under which the National Commission for Minorities is a statutory body, enacted?
x: The NCM is statutory under the NCM Act, 1992 and was set up on 17 May 1993.

s: The implementation of which Act does the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis monitor?
x: The NCSK monitors the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013; the NCPCR monitors RTE, POCSO and JJ Acts.

s: In January 2022, up to which date was the tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis extended?
x: In January 2022 the NCSK was extended for three years beyond 31 March 2022, that is, to 31 March 2025.

s: Up to which date has the tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis been extended most recently?
x: After the January 2022 extension to 31 March 2025, the NCSK was extended again up to 31 March 2028.

s: Under which Act are State Human Rights Commissions established?
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
x: SHRCs are set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; human-rights functions in Delhi remain with the NHRC.

s: Under the 2019 amendment, who may be appointed Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission?
o: A former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court
Only a serving Chief Justice of India
x: After the 2019 amendment, the Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court.

s: Into which matters may a State Human Rights Commission inquire?
o: Any matter regardless of its legislative list
The State List or the Concurrent List and is not already before the NHRC or another statutory commission
Only matters already decided by a court
x: The jurisdiction of an SHRC extends to matters in the State List and Concurrent List, but it cannot inquire into a matter already pending before the NHRC or another statutory commission.

s: By whom are the Chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission appointed and removed, respectively?
x: The Governor appoints SHRC members on the recommendation of a committee of the Chief Minister, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition (plus the Council Chairman and its LoP where a Council exists). Only the President can remove them. A reverses the two roles. The Chief Minister chairs the committee but does not appoint, and the State Legislature has no power to remove.

s: In which city does the Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission function?
x: The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission works from Kurnool.

s: Who among the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission?
x: The committee has the CM, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition; the Governor only appoints.

s: To whom are reports of State commissions constituted under State laws submitted?
o: Governor and laid before the State Legislature
Chief Minister and laid before the Union Cabinet
High Court and laid before the Legislative Council only
x: Reports of State commissions go to the Governor and are laid before the State Legislature.

s: Which of the following correctly explains the relevance of Articles 338(9) and 338A(10)?
o: They directly establish all State commissions.
They empower the President to appoint all State commission members.
They transfer the reports of State commissions to Parliament.
They require the Union and States to consult the concerned National Commission on policy matters affecting the communities concerned.
x: Articles 338(9) and 338A(10) concern consultation with the National Commissions on major policy matters; they do not create State commissions.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for SCs and STs reconstituted?
x: The AP SC/ST Commission, created by a 2003 Act, was reconstituted in 2016.

s: Under an Act of which year was the Andhra Pradesh Commission for Backward Classes set up?
x: The AP BC Commission is a permanent body under the AP Commission for BCs Act, 1993.

s: Who chairs the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes?
x: K.S. Jawahar chairs the AP SC Commission; Rayapati Sailaja chairs the AP State Commission for Women.

s: Under which Act was the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women set up?
o: AP Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
x: The AP State Commission for Women works under the Andhra Pradesh Women's Commission Act, 1998 (Act No. 9 of 1998).

s: Where does the office of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women function?
x: The AP Women's Commission office is at Mangalagiri (Guntur district); the AP SHRC is at Kurnool.

s: Who is the Chairperson of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women?
x: Rayapati Sailaja is the Chairperson of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women.

s: In which year did Maharashtra establish the first Lokayukta in India?
x: Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971, after the first Lokpal Bill (1968) and before the first Lokpal (2019).

s: Where are the recommendations of Lokayuktas binding?
x: Lokayukta recommendations are advisory in many States and binding only in some, not in every State.

s: Within what period did the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act require every State to establish a Lokayukta?
o: Six months of the Act’s assent
Two years of the first Lokpal appointment
One year of the commencement of the Act
Five years of the establishment of the Central Vigilance Commission
x: Every State was required to set up a Lokayukta within one year of the commencement of the Act.

s: To whom is the annual consolidated report of a State Lokayukta submitted?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The Lokayukta submits an annual consolidated report to the Governor.

s: Under which of the following are State Lokayuktas in India established?
o: A single central law under which the Union appoints them
An order of the Chief Justice of India
A direct provision of the Constitution
x: Each State sets up its Lokayukta under its own Act, so jurisdiction and coverage differ among States.

s: Which of the following pairs of State and Lokayukta arrangement is correctly matched?
o: Uttar Pradesh — Officials designated as Lokpal
x: Punjab has officials designated as Lokpal. Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have only a Lokayukta, while Maharashtra has a Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta.

s: With whom was the Bellary illegal iron ore mining report of 2011 associated?
x: The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report was prepared under Justice N. Santosh Hegde in 2011.

s: The Karnataka Lokayukta, which has its own Lokayukta Police wing, was established under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act of which year?
x: The Karnataka Lokayukta was established under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984, with its own police wing.

s: A major institutional weakness of many Lokayuktas is that they
o: have no independent investigating wing and depend on the State police or Anti-Corruption Bureau
submit all reports directly to Parliament
have no statutory basis in any State
x: Many Lokayuktas lack an independent investigating wing and therefore depend on the State police or the Anti-Corruption Bureau for investigation.

s: Which State was the first to pass a Lokayukta law, in 1970?
x: Odisha passed the first law (1970) but set up the institution only in 1983; Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta (1971).

s: Which Section of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 requires every State to set up a Lokayukta?
x: Section 63 requires every State to set up a Lokayukta by its own law within one year.

s: Which of the following States has a Lokayukta only, without an Upa-Lokayukta?
x: Bihar, UP and HP have a Lokayukta only; Karnataka, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and AP have both.

s: In which of the following States is the Chief Minister excluded from the Lokayukta's jurisdiction?
x: The CM is excluded in Maharashtra (also UP, Rajasthan, Bihar and AP) but included in MP, Gujarat, HP and Odisha.

s: By 2013, how many States had Lokayuktas?
x: By 2013, 21 States and 1 UT (Delhi) had Lokayuktas.

s: Which of the following pairs of State and year of its Lokayukta is correctly matched?
x: Bihar's Lokayukta dates to 1973; Karnataka is 1984, UP 1975 and Assam 1986.

s: Whose arrest followed the Bellary illegal iron ore mining report (2011)?
x: Justice N. Santosh Hegde's Bellary report led to the arrest of former minister G. Janardhana Reddy.

s: Which State reduced the tenure of its Lokayukta from eight years to five years?
x: Rajasthan cut the Lokayukta's tenure from 8 to 5 years.

s: While appointing a Lokayukta, the Governor generally consults the Leader of the Opposition and which other authority?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The Governor consults the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Leader of the Opposition, not the Chief Election Commissioner.

s: In which year did the Lok Sabha pass the First Lokpal Bill?
x: The First Lokpal Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha, was passed by it in 1969 and lapsed on the dissolution of that Lok Sabha.

s: In which year did Parliament pass the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill?
x: Parliament passed the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill in December 2013: the Rajya Sabha on 17 December and the Lok Sabha on 18 December 2013. The President gave assent on 1 January 2014.

s: Which of the following describes the status of the Lokpal?
o: Body created by a Constitutional Amendment
x: The Lokpal is established by statute and is not a constitutional body.

s: After the 2016 amendment, the form and manner of asset declaration under the Lokpal law is prescribed by which of the following?
x: The 2016 amendment kept the declaration but left its form and manner to be prescribed by the Central Government.

s: On which date did the Lokpal actually begin functioning?
x: Although the Act came into force in 2014, the Lokpal began functioning on 27 March 2019 after its Chairperson and members were appointed.

s: Why did the first Lokpal Bill, passed by the Lok Sabha in 1969, lapse?
o: The Lok Sabha was dissolved before the Rajya Sabha passed it
The Supreme Court struck it down
x: The 1968 Bill passed the Lok Sabha in 1969 but lapsed when that House was dissolved before the Rajya Sabha passed it.

s: Who introduced the Lokpal Bill, 2011 in the Lok Sabha on 4 August 2011?
x: V. Narayanasamy, Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, introduced the Lokpal Bill, 2011 in the Lok Sabha.

s: Who chaired the Standing Committee that examined the Lokpal Bill, 2011?
x: The Standing Committee on Public Grievances, Law and Justice was chaired by Abhishek Manu Singhvi; L.M. Singhvi coined the term Lokpal.

s: Which House passed the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill first, on 17 December 2013?
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
Neither; it was issued as an Ordinance
x: The Rajya Sabha passed it with amendments on 17 December 2013 and the Lok Sabha on 18 December 2013.

s: Under the original Lokpal Act, a public servant had to declare assets and liabilities within how many days of entering office?
x: The original Act required the declaration within 30 days of entering office.

s: After the first Lokpal Bill of 1968, how many times was a Lokpal Bill re-introduced and allowed to lapse up to 2008?
x: Bills were re-introduced in 1971, 1977, 1985, 1989, 1996, 1998, 2001, 2005 and 2008 - nine times, and all lapsed.

s: The first Lokpal Bill of 1968 was introduced during which Lok Sabha?
x: The first Lokpal Bill was introduced in 1968 in the 4th Lok Sabha; it lapsed when that House was dissolved.

s:
Consider the following statements about the first Lokpal Bill:
1. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha in 1968.
2. It was passed by both Houses of Parliament in 1969.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Bill was introduced in 1968 and passed only by the Lok Sabha in 1969; it lapsed before the Rajya Sabha passed it.

s: On which date did the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 receive the President's assent?
x: The President gave assent on 1 January 2014; the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.

s: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 came into force on 16 January 2014. Which event relating to the Act took place on 1 January 2014?
x: 1 January 2014 is the date of the President's assent; the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.

s:
Arrange the following events relating to the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 in chronological order:
1. President's assent
2. Passage by the Lok Sabha
3. Coming into force
4. Passage by the Rajya Sabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Rajya Sabha passed it on 17 Dec 2013, Lok Sabha on 18 Dec 2013, assent came on 1 Jan 2014 and it came into force on 16 Jan 2014.

s: Besides creating the Lokpal, the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 amended which Act to provide a Directorate of Prosecution for the CBI?
x: The 2013 Act also amended the DSPE Act, bringing the committee to select the CBI Director and a Directorate of Prosecution.

s: Who coined the term ‘Lokpal’?
x: The word ‘Lokpal’ was coined by Dr. L.M. Singhvi.

s: The institution of Ombudsman was first established in which country in 1809?
x: The Ombudsman institution was first set up in Sweden in 1809. Sweden’s 1766 law is associated with the right to information, not the origin of the Ombudsman institution.

s: What are the Indian equivalents of the Ombudsman at the Union and State levels respectively?
x: Lokpal is the Ombudsman institution at the Union level, while Lokayukta performs the corresponding role at the State level.

s: Which bodies did the Santhanam Committee recommend setting up?
x: The Santhanam Committee recommended the CVC and the CBI; the Lokpal-Lokayukta system came from the First ARC.

s: In which year did the First Administrative Reforms Commission recommend a two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta system?
x: The First ARC made the recommendation in 1966; the Second ARC reiterated it in 2007.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Administrative Reforms Commission – set up in 1966
First Administrative Reforms Commission – recommended the CVC and the CBI
x: The First ARC was set up in 1966 and recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas. The Ombudsman began in Sweden in 1809, and the term Lokpal was coined by Dr. L.M. Singhvi.

s: Who was the first chairman of the First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966)?
x: Morarji Desai first chaired the First ARC; K. Hanumanthaiya chaired it later.

s: Which report of the First ARC (1966) first recommended State Lokayuktas?
o: Problems of Redressal of Citizens' Grievances
x: The First ARC report 'Problems of Redressal of Citizens' Grievances' (1966) first recommended State Lokayuktas.

s: In which year was the term 'Lokpal' coined?
x: Dr. L.M. Singhvi coined the term Lokpal in 1963.

s: Sweden's law of 1766 is regarded as the world's first example of which of the following?
x: Sweden's 1766 law was a right to information law; its Ombudsman came in 1809.

s: Which body reiterated the recommendation for a Lokpal in 2007?
x: The Second ARC (2007) reiterated the Lokpal; the First ARC (1966) had first recommended it.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, which authority deals with complaints against functionaries other than the higher functionaries?
x: In AP the Lokayukta deals with higher functionaries and the Upa-Lokayukta with the remaining functionaries.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act enacted?
x: The governing law is the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983.

s: Which one of the following is the principal role of the Anti-Corruption Bureau in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Receiving complaints and submitting recommendations to the Governor
Investigating offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases
Advising departments on disciplinary matters without investigating offences
Exercising superintendence over the Central Bureau of Investigation in all cases
x: The Anti-Corruption Bureau is a police investigating agency that investigates Prevention of Corruption Act offences, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Lokayukta in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The AP Lokayukta offers informal procedure, easy access, almost free and prompt service, and independence from executive control. Interpreting the Constitution is not one of its features (APPSC 2019 PYQ).

s: Who appointed Justice (retd.) T. Mallikarjuna Rao as Lokayukta of Andhra Pradesh in August 2026?
o: Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court
x: Governor S. Abdul Nazeer appointed him under Section 3(1) on the recommendation of the Selection Committee.

s: From which year was the State Vigilance Commission in Andhra Pradesh set up on the pattern of the CVC?
x: The AP State Vigilance Commission was set up from 1964 on the CVC pattern; trap cases are handled by the Anti-Corruption Bureau.

s: To which city was the principal seat of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta shifted in 2021?
x: After bifurcation the AP Lokayukta worked from Hyderabad and shifted to Kurnool in 2021.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta:
1. After bifurcation, it worked from Hyderabad.
2. The AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983 was amended in 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: it worked from Hyderabad until its move to Kurnool in 2021, and the 1983 Act was amended in 2024.

s: For what term was Justice (Retd) T. Mallikarjuna Rao appointed AP Lokayukta in August 2026?
x: He was appointed under Section 3(1) for a 5-year term under Section 5.

s: Who was the first Lokayukta of integrated Andhra Pradesh?
x: Justice A. Sambasiva Rao was the first Lokayukta of the combined State of Andhra Pradesh.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Lokayukta of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Chief Minister comes within its ambit.
2. MLAs come within its ambit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The AP Lokayukta Act, 1983 defines 'Minister' as other than the Chief Minister, so the CM is outside its ambit; MLAs are covered – only statement 2 is correct.

s: On whose recommendation was the Central Vigilance Commission set up in 1964?
x: The CVC originated from the Santhanam Committee and was set up in 1964 by executive resolution.

s: Under the CVC Act of which year did the Central Vigilance Commission become a statutory body?
x: The Vineet Narain case (1997) directed statutory status, given by the CVC Act, 2003.

s: Which of the following is a member of the committee that selects the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
x: The CVC selection committee has the PM, the Home Minister and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Vigilance Commission?
o: It was set up in 1964 by an executive resolution
It became statutory under the CVC Act, 2003
It supervises the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases generally
x: The CVC is a statutory body, not a constitutional one.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission:
1. Its members hold office for 4 years or until the age of 65.
2. It supervises the CBI only in cases referred to it by the Lokpal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the CVC supervises the CBI in PCA cases generally; supervision only in referred cases is the Lokpal's role.

s: Besides the Central Vigilance Commissioner, how many Vigilance Commissioners at most can the Central Vigilance Commission have?
x: The CVC has the Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners.

s: Which Supreme Court case directed that the Central Vigilance Commission be given statutory status?
o: Vineet Narain v Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai v Union of India
Indra Sawhney v Union of India
x: The Vineet Narain case (1997) directed statutory status for the CVC, which came with the CVC Act, 2003.

s: On which date did the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 receive the President's assent?
x: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act (Act No. 17 of 2014) got assent on 9 May 2014.

s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, a whistle blower is a person who makes which of the following?
o: Request for information under the RTI Act
Complaint about service matters to the Lokpal
Public interest disclosure about corruption or wilful misuse of power by a public servant
x: A whistle blower makes a public interest disclosure about corruption or wilful misuse of power by a public servant.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014:
1. Anonymous complaints are not taken up.
2. Complaints are barred after 7 years.
3. An appeal lies to the Supreme Court within 60 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the appeal lies to the High Court within 60 days.

s: Who is the competent authority under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 for complaints about central government employees?
x: For central employees, the Central Vigilance Commission is the competent authority under the 2014 Act.

s: What was the status of the Central Vigilance Commission when it was first set up in 1964?
o: A statutory body under the CVC Act
A body under the DSPE Act
x: The CVC was set up by executive resolution in 1964 and became statutory only in 2003.

s: The Central Vigilance Commission consists of the Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than how many Vigilance Commissioners?
x: The CVC has the Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners, holding office for four years or until 65.

s: Which body is the competent authority under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act?
x: The CVC is the competent authority under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act; it is a statutory, not constitutional, body.

s: Who chairs the Selection Committee of the Lokpal?
o: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: The Prime Minister chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee; the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member at all.

s: An eminent person must have at least how many years' experience in specified fields to be appointed Chairperson of the Lokpal?
x: Besides a former CJI or Supreme Court judge, an eminent person with 25 years' relevant experience may be Lokpal Chairperson.

s: What is the term of office of the Chairperson or a member of the Lokpal?
o: six years irrespective of age, with one reappointment
eight years or until attaining 70 years of age, whichever is later
five years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is later, with reappointment permitted
five years or until attaining 70 years of age, whichever is earlier, with no reappointment
x: The term is five years or until the age of 70, whichever is earlier, and reappointment is not permitted. A member may become Chairperson within the total five-year period.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Lokpal is correct?
o: The Lokpal may inquire into a complaint filed at any time after the alleged offence.
A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal may simultaneously be an MP or MLA.
The Act applies only to public servants posted within India.
A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal cannot be an MP or MLA.
x: A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal cannot be a Member of Parliament or a Member of a Legislative Assembly. The Act also covers public servants outside India and bars complaints filed after seven years from the alleged offence.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee?
x: The Rajya Sabha Chairman is not a member; the PM chairs the committee, and the Speaker and the CJI (or a Supreme Court judge he nominates) are members.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Lokpal Selection Committee is correctly matched?
o: Chairman of the Rajya Sabha – Member
Speaker of the Lok Sabha – Chairperson
Eminent jurist – nominated by the Chief Justice of India
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha – Member
x: The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member. The PM is the chair, the Rajya Sabha Chairman is not a member, and the eminent jurist is nominated by the President.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Search Committee for the Lokpal?
o: It prepares a panel for consideration
It is constituted by the Selection Committee
It may have fewer than seven persons
At least half its members must be from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women
x: The Search Committee must have at least seven persons.

s: The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and not more than how many members?
x: The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to eight members, at least half of whom must be judicial members.

s: What share of the members of the Lokpal must be judicial members?
x: Half the members of the Lokpal are judicial members, and at least half are from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women.

s: What is the minimum age for appointment as Chairperson or member of the Lokpal?
x: A Lokpal Chairperson or member must be at least 45 years old.

s: The Search Committee for the Lokpal consists of at least how many persons?
x: The Selection Committee sets up a Search Committee of at least 7 persons, half from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women.

s: Who appoints the Chairperson and members of the Lokpal?
x: The President appoints them on the recommendation of the Selection Committee.

s: At least what share of the members of the Lokpal must be from the SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women?
x: At least 50% of Lokpal members must be from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women; separately, 50% must be judicial members.

s:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Lokpal:
1. Half of its members must be judicial members.
2. At least half of its members must be from the SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both rules apply together: 50% judicial members and at least 50% from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women.

s: The Inquiry Wing of the Lokpal conducts preliminary inquiry into offences under which Act?
x: The Inquiry Wing conducts preliminary inquiries into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
o: Central officials of Groups A, B, C and D — Group C and D complaints are referred to the CVC
Members of Parliament — all speeches and votes in Parliament are subject to inquiry
NGOs — covered only when they receive foreign contribution below ₹10 lakh
Indian public servants abroad — excluded because jurisdiction ends outside India
x: The Lokpal’s jurisdiction covers central officials of Groups A, B, C and D, while complaints against Group C and D officials are sent to the CVC, which reports back to the Lokpal. Parliamentary speeches and votes are excluded, NGOs are covered above the stated threshold, and public servants outside India are included.

s: Which of the following categories of organisations comes within the Lokpal’s jurisdiction when the stated condition is fulfilled?
o: Only organisations receiving domestic donations above ₹10 lakh
Only constitutional bodies receiving no government funding
Every private company, irrespective of funding
NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh
x: NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh come within the stated jurisdiction of the Lokpal.

s: Allegations against the Prime Minister relating to which of the following are excluded from the Lokpal's jurisdiction?
o: International relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space
x: All these areas, namely international relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space, are excluded from the Lokpal's jurisdiction over the Prime Minister.

s: What majority of the full Bench of the Lokpal is required to approve an inquiry against the Prime Minister?
x: An inquiry against the PM needs full-Bench approval by at least two-thirds, and it is held in camera.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
o: It applies to Indian public servants both within and outside India
It extends to Union Ministers and Members of Parliament
It covers anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament
It covers bodies set up by an Act of Parliament or funded by the government
x: Anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament is outside the Lokpal's jurisdiction.

s: Within how many days is a preliminary inquiry under the Lokpal framework ordinarily to be completed?
x: A preliminary inquiry ordinarily takes 90 days, extendable by 90 more days for reasons recorded in writing.

s: Within what period is a trial by the Special Court under the Lokpal framework ordinarily to be completed?
o: six months, extendable by six months
one year, extendable up to two years
x: The Special Court trial has a one-year limit extendable up to two years. Six months plus six months is the investigation limit; 90 plus 90 days is the preliminary inquiry; 60 days is the Inquiry Wing's report.

s: Which of the following does Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 require to be established?
o: a vigilance wing headed by the CVC and an audit wing headed by the CAG
an inquiry wing headed by a Director of Inquiry and a prosecution wing headed by a Director of Prosecution
a judicial wing headed by the Chief Justice of India and a police wing headed by the CBI Director
a parliamentary wing headed by the Speaker and a prosecution wing headed by the Attorney General
x: Section 11 of the Lokpal Act provides for the Inquiry Wing, headed by a Director of Inquiry; the Lokpal also has a Prosecution Wing headed by a Director of Prosecution. The other options name bodies that are not wings of the Lokpal.

s: When can property acquired by corrupt means be attached and confiscated under the Lokpal law?
o: Even while the prosecution is pending
Only after the prosecution is over
Only after the Supreme Court confirms conviction
x: The Lokpal can attach and confiscate tainted property even while the prosecution is pending.

s: In which cases does the Lokpal exercise superintendence and direction over the CBI?
o: All Prevention of Corruption Act cases
All cases investigated by the CBI
Only the cases referred by the Lokpal
Only cases against State Government employees
x: The Lokpal supervises the CBI only in cases it refers; the CVC supervises it in Prevention of Corruption Act cases generally.

s: A complaint is made more than seven years after the alleged offence. What is the position of the Lokpal on such a complaint under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: can inquire only if the complaint concerns a Union Minister
cannot inquire into it after the statutory seven-year period
can inquire only after approval of the Rajya Sabha Chairman
must inquire into it because there is no limitation period
x: The Lokpal cannot inquire into a complaint made after seven years from the alleged offence.

s: Under the Lokpal Act, to which body are complaints against Group C and D central officials sent?
x: Group C and D complaints go to the CVC, which reports back to the Lokpal.

s: What is the position of public servants posted outside India under the Lokpal Act?
o: Covered only if they belong to Group A
Covered only with the consent of the host country
x: The Lokpal covers public servants both in and outside India.

s: Within what period is an investigation under the Lokpal framework ordinarily to be completed?
x: Investigation: 6 months + 6 months. The preliminary inquiry is 90 + 90 days and the trial 1 year up to 2 years.

s: Within how many days must the Inquiry Wing of the Lokpal submit its report after a reference?
x: The Inquiry Wing reports within 60 days of the reference.

s: In respect of which of the following are Union Ministers and MPs excluded from the Lokpal's jurisdiction?
o: All acts done while in office
Anything said or any vote given in Parliament
x: Ministers and MPs are covered, but not for anything said or any vote given in Parliament.

s: With which issue is Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act associated?
o: Publication of the Corruption Perceptions Index
Appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner
General consent of States for all CBI investigations
Prior approval before investigating certain decisions or recommendations by public servants
x: Section 17A concerns prior approval for investigation in specified circumstances involving decisions or recommendations of public servants. Its interpretation has been the subject of a Supreme Court split verdict and debate over 'sanction paralysis'.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: First Lokpal — Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose
Lokpal inquiry and prosecution wings — fully staffed from the commencement of the Act
Group C and D complaints — Central Vigilance Commission
x: The Lokpal’s inquiry wing under Section 11 and its prosecution wing were reported as still not fully staffed. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Who has been the second Chairperson of the Lokpal since 10 March 2024?
x: Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the second Chairperson of the Lokpal on 10 March 2024.

s:
Assertion (A): The first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968.
Reason (R): Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was the first Lokpal of India.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but unrelated: the first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968, while Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became the first Lokpal only in 2019 under the 2013 Act.

s: In the January 2026 split verdict of the Supreme Court on Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which judge held Section 17A unconstitutional?
x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna held Section 17A unconstitutional. Justice K.V. Viswanathan upheld prior approval only if based on a binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta. Khanwilkar is the Lokpal Chairperson and Surya Kant the CJI; neither was part of the split.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: State Vigilance Commission — Set up from 1964 on the CVC pattern
x: Section 17A belongs to the Prevention of Corruption Act and concerns prior approval before investigation. The Lokpal Inquiry Wing is associated with Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act.

s: Which post did Sushil Chandra, a non-judicial member of the Lokpal, hold earlier?
x: Sushil Chandra, a former Chief Election Commissioner, is a non-judicial member of the Lokpal.

s: In which year was the first Lokpal of India appointed?
x: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was appointed the first Lokpal on 19 March 2019.

s: Before becoming the first Lokpal of India, Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was a retired judge of which court?
x: The first Lokpal, Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, was a retired Supreme Court judge.

s: According to the Union Government's reply in the Lok Sabha (March 2026), how many complaints did the Lokpal register in 2024-25?
x: The Lokpal registered 292 complaints in 2024-25 and disposed of 260 of them.

s:
Consider the following statements about complaints to the Lokpal:
1. The Lokpal registered 292 complaints in 2024-25.
2. Complaints registered in 2025-26 (up to February 2026) were fewer than in 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 292 complaints were registered in 2024-25; 389 were registered in 2025-26 up to February 2026, so complaints rose.

s: Who led the India Against Corruption movement?
x: India Against Corruption was led by Anna Hazare and was central to the 2011 civil society campaign for the Jan Lokpal Bill.

s: Who chaired the Joint Drafting Committee on the Lokpal Bill (April 2011)?
x: Pranab Mukherjee chaired the Joint Drafting Committee; Shanti Bhushan was its co-chair.

s: Where was Anna Hazare's fast of April 2011 for the Jan Lokpal Bill held?
x: The April 2011 fast was at Jantar Mantar; the August 2011 fast was at Ramlila Maidan.

s: Who was the co-chairman of the Joint Drafting Committee on the Lokpal Bill set up in April 2011?
x: The Joint Drafting Committee (April 2011) was chaired by Pranab Mukherjee with Shanti Bhushan as co-chairman.

s: On whose recommendation was the Central Bureau of Investigation set up in 1963?
o: Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption
x: The CBI was set up in 1963 following the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption, constituted during 1962–64.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Bureau of Investigation?
o: It is an attached office under the Department of Personnel and Training
It derives its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946
It was initially set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs
x: The CBI is not a constitutional body; it was set up by an MHA resolution and draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946.

s: In which year was the Central Bureau of Investigation set up?
x: The CBI was set up in 1963, after the Special Police Establishment (1941) and the DSPE Act (1946), and a year before the CVC (1964).

s: By a resolution of which Ministry was the CBI set up on 1 April 1963?
x: The CBI was set up by an MHA resolution; it is now an attached office under the Ministry of Personnel.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Central Bureau of Investigation
B. Delhi Special Police Establishment Act
C. Special Police Establishment
D. Central Vigilance Commission
x: SPE (1941), DSPE Act (1946), CBI (1963) and CVC (1964).

s: Who make up the committee on whose recommendation the Central Government appoints the Director of the CBI?
o: Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Attorney General of India
Union Home Minister, Leader of the largest opposition party and CVC
Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and CVC
Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India or his nominee
x: The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha or leader of the largest opposition party, and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by the CJI.

s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised criticism or debate about the functioning of the CBI?
o: The ‘caged parrot’ description due to executive control
A constitutional bar on the CBI investigating economic offences
x: No constitutional bar stops the CBI from investigating economic offences; it does handle them. The other three are recognised criticisms or debates.

s: What is the minimum tenure of the Director of the CBI?
x: The CBI Director has a minimum tenure of two years, extendable up to five years since 2021.

s: For what term is the Director of Prosecution of the CBI appointed on the CVC's recommendation?
x: The Director of Prosecution is appointed on the CVC's recommendation for a two-year term.

s: Who was the founder Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation?
x: D.P. Kohli was the founder Director of the CBI (APPSC 2018 key); an annual memorial lecture is held in his name. K. Santhanam headed the committee that recommended the CBI; Vineet Narain was the petitioner in the 1997 case; Vohra headed the 1993 committee on the criminal-politician nexus.

s: Through which Act was the present procedure of selecting the CBI Director by a committee headed by the Prime Minister introduced?
x: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 amended the DSPE framework and introduced the present three-member selection committee. Until 2014, the process operated under the DSPE Act alone.

s: The CBI is an attached office under which Ministry?
x: The CBI is under the Ministry of Personnel (DoPT); ED and DRI are under Finance.

s: Which body recommended a new law to replace the DSPE Act for the CBI?
x: The Second ARC (2007) recommended a new law to replace the DSPE Act.

s: Up to what maximum total period can the tenure of the CBI Director be extended under the 2021 changes?
x: The CBI Director has a minimum 2-year tenure, extendable one year at a time up to 5 years (2021).

s: The 2021 change allowing tenure extension one year at a time up to five years applies to the CBI Director and which other office?
o: Director of Prosecution of the CBI
x: Since 2021 both the CBI Director and the ED Director can get one-year extensions up to five years in all.

s: The decision in Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1997) is associated with which of the following changes concerning the CBI?
o: Transfer of CBI control to the Ministry of Finance and a five-year tenure
Transfer of all CBI investigations to the Enforcement Directorate
Abolition of State consent and appointment of the Director by the Lokpal
Superintendence by the CVC and a fixed two-year tenure for the CBI Director
x: The 1997 Vineet Narain judgment gave the CVC superintendence over the CBI and prescribed a fixed two-year tenure for the CBI Director. The DSPE Act was revised accordingly in 2003.

s: After the Vineet Narain judgment, who decides whether a case is to be investigated by the CBI?
x: The judgment did not give investigation decisions to the CVC; the CBI alone decides whether to investigate.

s: In which year was Vineet Narain v. Union of India decided?
x: Vineet Narain was decided in 1997; the DSPE Act was revised in 2003 in response to its directions.

s: What did the Vineet Narain judgment (1997) quash?
x: Vineet Narain quashed the Single Directive that required prior sanction to probe senior officers.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the CBI is correctly matched?
o: OCSAE Unit — Routing requests for international police assistance
CBI — India’s National Central Bureau for Interpol
BHARATPOL portal — Handling bank securities and fraud
Economic Offences cells — Investigating online child sexual abuse material
x: The CBI is India’s National Central Bureau for Interpol. OCSAE handles online child sexual abuse material, BHARATPOL routes international assistance requests, and the economic offences cells handle bank securities and fraud.

s: With whom is the anti-corruption work of the CBI mainly concerned?
o: Central Government and Union Territory employees and their public sector undertakings
Foreign diplomatic personnel stationed in India
Only elected representatives of State Legislatures
x: The CBI’s anti-corruption mandate mainly covers Central Government and Union Territory employees and their public sector undertakings.

s: What does the CBI's OCSAE Prevention/Investigation Unit, set up in 2019, deal with?
x: The OCSAE unit (2019) acts against online child sexual abuse material.

s: For Interpol, the CBI serves as which of the following for India?
x: The CBI is India's National Central Bureau for Interpol.

s: Who launched the BHARATPOL portal on 7 January 2025?
x: BHARATPOL, developed by the CBI, was launched by Home Minister Amit Shah on 7 January 2025.

s: Why does the Central Bureau of Investigation need the consent of a State Government under Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946?
o: The CBI is constitutionally subordinate to State Governments
Criminal law is exclusively a Union subject
Police is a subject in the State List
The Lokpal Act prohibits investigation without State approval
x: Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires general or specific consent of the State concerned because police is included in Entry 2 of the State List.

s: When did Andhra Pradesh withdraw general consent to the CBI?
x: AP withdrew general consent in November 2018 and restored it in June 2019.

s: The CBI needs State consent because 'police' falls under which entry of the State List?
x: Police is Entry 2 of the State List, so Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires State consent.

s: Which body leads the committee that recommends CBI officers of the rank of Superintendent of Police and above?
x: A CVC-led committee recommends CBI officers of SP rank and above; the CVC does not, however, conduct trials of CBI cases.

s: Under which Act did the Central Vigilance Commission, set up in 1964 by executive resolution, become a statutory body?
x: The CVC became statutory under the CVC Act, 2003; it is the apex vigilance body but not a constitutional body.

s: Under the 2023 Act, on whose recommendation does the President appoint the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners?
o: the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India
x: The 2023 Act panel is the PM, a Union Cabinet Minister and the LoP in the Lok Sabha. The CJI is not a member (option B is the CBI Director panel pattern); option C wrongly adds the Speaker and CJI; the Cabinet alone does not recommend.

s: Who make up the committee on whose recommendation the President appoints the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
o: Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Union Home Minister, Union Law Minister and Cabinet Secretary
x: The CVC panel is PM, Union Home Minister and LoP in the Lok Sabha. Option B mixes in the Lokpal panel's Speaker and CJI; option C is the CBI Director panel; option D is not any statutory panel.

s: Who make up the committee on whose recommendation the President appoints the Chief Information Commissioner at the Centre?
o: Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Union Home Minister
Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
x: The CIC panel is PM, LoP in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM; the CJI is not a member. Option D is the CVC panel; options A and C mix in members of other panels.

s: Who appoints the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
x: The Central Vigilance Commissioner is appointed by the President, not the Prime Minister.

s: Who appoints the State Information Commissioners?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The CIC is appointed by the President and the SIC by the Governor.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends the State Chief Information Commissioner?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly
Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister
x: The SIC panel is the CM, the LoP in the Assembly and a CM-nominated minister; the Chief Justice is not a member.

s: Who appoints the Director of the CBI?
x: The Central Government appoints the CBI Director on the recommendation of a committee of the PM, LoP and CJI (or his nominee).

s: Under Section 5 of the RTI Act, who designates Public Information Officers?
x: Each public authority designates its own Public Information Officers under Section 5.

s: What did the Vohra Committee (1993) examine?
o: the nexus between criminals, politicians and bureaucrats
the setting up of the Central Bureau of Investigation
the creation of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas
the tenure of the CBI Director
x: The Vohra Committee (1993) dealt with the criminal-politician-bureaucrat nexus. The CBI came from the Santhanam Committee; Lokpal/Lokayukta from the First ARC; the CBI Director's tenure from Vineet Narain and later amendments.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's investigating agencies?
o: The Enforcement Directorate enforces the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002
The Enforcement Directorate enforces the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
The CBI handles only corruption cases and has no role in economic or special crimes
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence is mainly concerned with anti-smuggling and customs evasion
x: Apart from corruption cases, the CBI also investigates economic and special crimes.

s: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what can the Director of the Enforcement Directorate do?
o: Attach property believed to be proceeds of crime
Grant general consent to CBI investigations in a State
Appoint the Director of the CBI
x: Under the PMLA, the ED Director may attach property believed to be proceeds of crime.

s: The Enforcement Directorate functions under which Ministry/Department?
o: Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue
x: The ED is under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. The CBI is under the Ministry of Personnel (DoPT); the Home Ministry and Law Ministry do not control the ED.

s: Who publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index?
x: Transparency International publishes the CPI, scoring perceived public-sector corruption from 0 to 100.

s: What was India's rank in the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025?
x: India ranked 91st of 182 with a score of 39 in CPI 2025, up from 96th in 2024.

s: What does the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence mainly deal with?
x: The DRI handles anti-smuggling and customs evasion under the Finance Ministry's Department of Revenue.

s: Under which department was the Enforcement Directorate founded in 1956 as the 'Enforcement Unit'?
x: The ED began in 1956 as an Enforcement Unit under the Department of Economic Affairs; it is now under the Department of Revenue.

s: On what scale does the Corruption Perceptions Index score the perceived level of public-sector corruption?
x: Transparency International's CPI scores perceived public-sector corruption from 0 to 100.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Corruption Perceptions Index:
1. It measures the perceived level of public-sector corruption.
2. India's score in the CPI 2025 was 39.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The CPI measures perceived public-sector corruption, and India scored 39 (rank 91 of 182) in CPI 2025.

s: The Central Information Commission consists of the Chief Information Commissioner and up to how many Information Commissioners?
x: The CIC has the Chief Information Commissioner and up to 10 Information Commissioners.

s: The Central Information Commission was constituted in 2005 under which Section of the RTI Act?
x: The CIC was constituted on 12 October 2005 under Section 12 of the RTI Act.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 and the Rules of 2019?
o: The 2019 Rules fixed the term of an Information Commissioner at five years
The Centre was empowered to fix the tenure of CIC and SIC members
The Centre was empowered to fix the salaries of CIC and SIC members
The 2019 Rules fixed the term of an Information Commissioner at three years
x: The 2019 Rules fixed the term at three years, not five, using the power the 2019 Amendment gave the Centre to fix tenure and salaries.

s: An RTI application concerns a person's life or liberty. Within what time should the information ordinarily be provided?
x: When the application concerns life or liberty, information must be provided within 48 hours. The ordinary time limit is 30 days.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the RTI Act is correctly matched?
o: Section 8(1)(j) – personal information made mandatorily disclosable
RTI appeals involving personal data – transferred to the CVC
Section 8(1)(j) exemption – limited to information held by private companies
x: The DPDP Act, 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) to exempt personal information outright, removing the public-interest override.

s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 is associated with which of the following in relation to the RTI Act?
o: A call for its 're-examination', including a possible 'ministerial veto'
A proposal to extend RTI to all private companies
Restoration of the public-interest override in Section 8(1)(j)
Making the CIC a constitutional body
x: The Survey called for a re-examination of the RTI Act, suggesting exemptions for confidential service records and draft policy discussions and floating a possible ministerial veto. It did not propose extension to private companies, restoration of the override (removed by the DPDP Act) or constitutional status.

s: A State Information Commissioner may be removed by the Governor for proved misbehaviour after an inquiry by which body?
x: Under Section 17, removal follows a Supreme Court inquiry on the Governor's reference.

s: Who was the State Chief Information Commissioner of Andhra Pradesh in 2025?
x: R. Mahaboob Basha was AP's State Chief Information Commissioner in 2025.
